strategy.summary: Object-dtype arrays of bare numbers cast with astype to a timedelta64 unit (e.g. m8[s]) are read as nanoseconds and truncated to zero on the buggy commit 7cafb46e9665; the fix routes object->timedelta64 through the array constructor path (as datetime64 already does) so the unit applies. Reproduce by running the new pandas tests that assert astype matches the constructor and the frame/series m8[s] equality, which should fail on buggy and pass on fixed.

system_packages: a C/C++ compiler toolchain (gcc or clang) and git

strategy.reproducing_test: pandas/tests/series/methods/test_astype.py::test_astype_object_numeric_to_timedelta64_unit (parametrized over s, ms, us, ns) and the frame tests test_astype_object_numeric_to_timedelta64_unit_2d and test_astype_object_numeric_to_timedelta64_unit_2d_mixed from the developer's diff
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision 7cafb46e9665 the series test for unit s/ms fails because ser.astype('m8[s]') yields zeros while the constructor yields [2s, 3s], so assert_series_equal raises; the frame 2d tests likewise fail on the m8[s] comparison. On the fixed revision (PR #68688 applied) all these tests pass, with astype agreeing with the constructor for each unit.
strategy.numerical_probe: pd.Series([2, 3], dtype=object).astype('m8[s]') compared to pd.Series([2, 3], dtype='m8[s]'); buggy gives zeros, fixed gives 2 and 3 seconds
risks: Environment versions are unbounded in the evidence (NumPy, python-dateutil, tzdata, Cython have no documented constraint and no era ceiling); the strategy chooses current releases and this choice is not evidence-derived, so a NumPy scalar/casting change could alter the behaviour.

The defect is a pure Python/Cython logic path, not architecture-specific; no sanitiser or big-endian platform is stated as required, so it should reproduce on x86_64 Linux, but this is not confirmed by the evidence.

Multi-column object blocks: the fix is per-column, so the 2D mixed test depends on block layout; the test asserts len(_mgr.blocks)==1, which must hold on the buggy commit or the test errors instead of failing for the right reason.

Merge and error-message tests changed wording ('Supported timedelta64 resolutions'); those tests may fail on the fixed revision if the message is not exact, and they are not part of the core transition.
Build requires compiling Cython extensions; editable build flags from the project are assumed and the buggy commit must build cleanly before the test can be trusted.

oracle.reference_source: pd.Series(values, dtype='m8[unit]') constructor path, as in the developer's tests
oracle.why: The tests compare astype output to the constructor result with assert_series_equal/assert_frame_equal, so equality is exact for integer-valued timedeltas.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: astype yields zero timedeltas instead of 2s/3s, so assert_series_equal/assert_frame_equal raises an AssertionError comparing values, because the buggy _astype_nansafe object->timedelta64 branch ignores the requested unit and reads the numbers as nanoseconds.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: astype delegates to the array constructor path which applies the requested unit, so result equals the constructor result for every unit and the frame column comparisons match.
